V.|OF THE APOSTLES.|303}}</noinclude>Sauiour God hath exalted vvith his right hand, to giue repentance to Israël, and remission of sinnes. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=32}}† and vve are vvitnesses of these vvordes, and the holy Ghost, vvhom God hath giuen to al that obey him. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=33}}† Vvhen they had heard these things, it cut them to the hart, and they consulted to kil them.

{{verse|chapter=5|verse=34}}† But one in the Councel rising vp, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a doctor of lavv honorable to al the people, commaunded the men to be put forth a vvhile. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=35}}† and he said to them, Ye men of Israël, take heede to your selues touching these men vvhat you meane to doe. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=36}}† For before these daies there rose {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Theudas''.}}∷ Theódas, saying he vvas some body, to vvhom consented a numbre of men about foure hundred, vvho vvas slaine: and al that beleeued him, vvere dispersed, and brought to nothing. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=37}}† After this fellovv there rose Iudas of Galilee in the daies of the Enrolling, and drevv avvay the people after him, and he perished: and as many as euer consented to him, vvere dispersed. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=38}}† And novv therfore I say to you, depart from these men and let them alone: for if this counsel or vvorke be of men, it vvil be dissolued: {{verse|chapter=5|verse=39}}† but if it be {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Time, and the euident successe of Christes Church and religion, proue it to be of God: no violence of the Iewes, no persecution of the Heathen Princes, no endeuour of domestical Aduersaries, heretikes, Schismatikes, or il liuers, preuailing against it. as on the other side, many attempts haue been made by Arius, Macedonius, Nestorius, Luther, & the like, who thought them selues to be some body: but after they had plaied their partes a while, their memory is buried, or liueth only in malediction & infamie, & their scholers come to naught Therfore let no Cath. man be scandalized that this heresie holdeth vp for a time. For the Arians & some others florished much longer then these, and were better supported by Princes and learning, & yet had an end.}}∷ of God, you are not able to dissolue {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`it'',}}`them', lest perhaps you be found to resist God also. And they consented to him. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=40}}† And calling in the Apostles, after they had scourged them, they charged them that they should not speake in the name of {{sc|Iesvs}}, and dimissed them. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=41}}† And they vvent from the sight of the councel reioycing, because they vvere accounted vvorthy to suffer reproche for the name of {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=42}}† And euery day they ceased not in the temple and from house to house to teach and euangelize Christ {{sc|Iesvs}}.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}

''2. Defrauded.''] In that (saith S. Augustine) {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. ser. 9. in append. de diuersis tom. 10''.}}he withdrew any part of that which he promised, he vvas guilty at once, both of sacrilege, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Sacrilege.}}and of fraude. of sacrilege, because he robbed God of that vvhich vvas his by promes: of fraude, in that he withheld of the whole gift, a peece. Let now the Heretikes come, and say it was for lying or hypocrisie onely that this facte vvas condemned: because they be loth to haue sacrilege counted any such sinne, who haue taught men not onely to take avvay from God some peece of that or al that them selues gaue, but plainly to spoile & apply to them selues al that other men gaue.

''3. Peter said.''] S. Peter (as you see here) without mans relation knew this fraude and the cogitations of Ananias, and as head of the College and of the whole Church against which this robbery vvas committed, executed this heauy sentence of Excommunication {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Excommunication ioyned vvith corporal paines.}}both against him, and his vvife consenting to the Sacrilege. for it was excommunication by S. Augustines iudgement, ''(li. 3 cont. ep. Parm. c. 1 to. 7'') and had this corporal miraculous death ioyned withal, as the<noinclude>{{rh|||Excommunication}}</noinclude>
